title: A Parish for the Verdict Revisited
premise: In the coastal parish of Kilbride, coroner Silas Halloran receives two letters about a drowning ruled accidental twenty years ago: one from a man confessing to murder, one promising a second death unless a witness named Ada Quinn comes forward. Silas knows Ada was buried years ago — or so he believed when he signed her certificate himself. As he reopens the inquest, he discovers his late mentor falsified records to protect the town's beloved priest, and that Ada may have staged her own death and still lives. The killer is the priest's devoted housekeeper, who has been eliminating everyone who knew the truth; the final letter was bait to draw out Ada. In the climax at the flooded quarry chapel, Silas must choose between shielding his community's memory of its sainted mentor and testifying to the truth, saving Ada but burying the man who taught him everything.
about_author: T. M. Hartwell is the pen name of a former rural court clerk who spent a decade transcribing small-town inquests before turning to fiction. They write mysteries steeped in parish life, where every secret has a gravestone.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Silas Halloran, sorting decades of parish records, opens twin letters arriving the same morning: a confession to the 2004 drowning of Tom Rafferty, and a threat promising more deaths if 'the witness' stays silent. His POV establishes his intimacy with the town's dead. The beat is unease — the handwriting on both letters is identical, and it belongs to someone he buried.

chapters.title: The Grave That Answers
chapters.summary: Silas exhumes his own memory: he certified Ada Quinn's death in 2005, yet the letters name her as living witness. He visits her grave and finds fresh flowers. Detective Maren Oduya arrives from the county, skeptical of reopening a closed case. POV alternates between Silas's dread and Maren's procedural suspicion. The emotional beat is vertigo — the ground itself seems to be lying.

chapters.title: What Father Brendan Kept
chapters.summary: Silas searches his dead mentor Father Brendan's rectory office and finds a locked ledger listing payments to three families after Rafferty's death. The town's saint had bought silence. Guilt curdles into anger as Silas realizes his own certification may have been quietly steered. Beat: betrayal — loyalty to a dead man begins to rot.

chapters.title: The Housekeeper's Rosary
chapters.summary: Maren interviews Bridie Nolan, Father Brendan's housekeeper for forty years, now caretaker of his legacy. Bridie is warm, grief-stricken, unimpeachable — and she quotes details from the confession letter no one released. Silas notices; Maren doesn't. Beat: quiet horror beneath civility as the reader sees what Silas almost misses.

chapters.title: A Drowning, Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Ada Quinn's voice: 2004, the night Tom Rafferty died at the quarry, what she saw, and why she let the parish believe she drowned herself a year later. Her love for Tom and terror of Bridie drive her underground. Beat: heartbreak — the witness everyone mourns chose erasure to survive.

chapters.title: Third Letter
chapters.summary: A third letter arrives — addressed not to police but to Silas personally, naming him as the next to die unless he stops digging. That night the archive room burns, destroying the original inquest file. Silas realizes the arsonist needed him alive long enough to be blamed. Beat: fear turning to resolve; Silas stops being an observer.

chapters.title: The Quarry Chapel
chapters.summary: Following the ledger's payment trail, Silas and Maren find the flooded quarry where a derelict boathouse-chapel holds Ada's hidden years: rationed supplies, newspaper clippings, letters never sent to Tom's mother. Someone has been feeding her — or watching her. Fresh bootprints lead out toward the road. Beat: tenderness interrupted by the realization Ada is being hunted right now.

chapters.title: Confession, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Bridie summons Silas to the rectory and confesses — partially. She killed Rafferty to protect Father Brendan from scandal over church funds, then spent twenty years 'keeping the parish clean,' including the second letter's victims. She believes she is doing holy work, and asks Silas, as Brendan's heir, for absolution. Beat: chilling intimacy — evil wearing devotion's face.

chapters.title: Vespers at the Waterline
chapters.summary: Climax. Silas decodes Ada's hiding place too late: Bridie reaches her first at the quarry chapel. Silas and Maren arrive as rising water traps them all; Silas chooses to testify aloud, recording the truth even as it damns his mentor, and pulls Ada from the water while Maren subdues Bridie. Beat: sacrifice — truth chosen over belonging, at real cost.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Resolution. The new inquest corrects two deaths and indicts a third; the town grieves its tarnished saint, and some neighbors turn from Silas for saying it plainly. Ada, finally visible, plants flowers on Tom's grave beside Silas. He reopens his ledger of names and adds none — only amends two. Beat: bittersweet peace — belonging rebuilt on truth rather than silence.
